children: Feeder cattle futures reached a two-week high on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange on Friday and live cattle also advanced due to demand from beef processors and expectations of higher cash prices, analysts said.
The markets have recovered since last week, when live cattle fell to the lowest price since December and feeder cattle touched the lowest level since September.

"The cattle market is shrugging off bearish news of lower cutouts and heavier weights, looking ahead to stronger cash trade possibly this week," said Brian Hoops, president of Midwest Market Solutions.
ended 3.675 cents higher at 335.350 cents per pound and set the highest price since October 30. The contract has advanced for five consecutive sessions.
ended up 1.750 cents at 220.650 cents per pound and reached the highest level since November 2.
Traders were waiting for details of transactions in the cash market. A week ago, weaker cash prices and fund selling dragged down futures.
"It appears the funds that liquidated positions are back to buying the futures," Hoops said.

Packer profits improved in recent weeks, helped by the recent dip in cattle prices. Beef packer margins were estimated at $34.40 per head, compared to losses of $20 per head last week, HedgersEdge said.

For pork processors, margins increased to $35.70 per hog from $22.45 a week ago, the firm said. Processors have benefited from low prices for hogs, but domestic and export demand for US pork has been weak.
US pork export sales were 39,500 metric tons in the week that ended on November 5, up 3% from the prior four-week average, the USDA said.
CME December lean hog futures (LHZ26) closed up 0.300 cent at 55.450 cents per pound after setting contract lows last week.
